minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  January 12, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
January 12, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:03 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority
PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas, other than the Public Hearing.
Caller (Name Unknown) spoke on Warrants and Bills, and the time limit that’s allotted
for public comments.

Gil Mathieu, District 4 resident, spoke on Agenda Item No. 7, Advance Funding
Agreement with Murphy’s Bowl LLC, and Closed Session Item No. CS-1, Labor
Negotiations with SEIU, IMEO, IEO, IPOA, IPMA, and IPCMA.

  1
 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  December 18, 2020, in the amount of $5,954,506.94, and dated January 07, 2021 in the
  amount of $3,253,256.74, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 21-04 INTRODUCED -
  AMENDMENT TO INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 11
  (BUILDING REGULATIONS). The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter
  was a public hearing to consider an ordinance amending Inglewood Municipal Code
  (IMC) Chapter 11, that notice had been given in the time, form and manner as required
  by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communications were received.

  Mandhir Singh, Building and Safety Manager, presented the staff report dated January
  12, 2021.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4 resident, commented on Solar Permitting and the roofing on the
  library.

  Mecca Carr, spoke regarding obtaining a permit to have a vigil in honor of Andrew
  Summerfield.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments at 2:13 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by
  Council Member Morales that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA 1)
  DELETING ARTICLE 17 (RESIDENTAL ROOFTOP SOLAR SYSTEM
  EXPEDITED PERMITTING) OF CHAPTER 11 IN ITS ENTIRETY
  AND REPLACING IT WITH AN UPDATED ARTICLE 17; 2) ADDING
  ARTICLE 18 (ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATION
  EXPEDITED PERMITTING) TO CHAPTER 11 (BUILDING
  REGULATIONS) TO ADOPT AN EXPEDITED, STREAMLINED
  PERMITTING PROCESS FOR ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING
  STATIONS AS REQUIRED BY LAW.

  was introduced by Council Member Morales with the following amendments to Chapter
  11 of the IMC: 1) DeleteArticle 17 (Residential Solar Permitting) in its entirety, and
  replacing it with an updated 17; and 2) Add Article 18 (Electric Vehicle Charging
  Stations Expedited Review Process) to adopt an expedited, streamlined permitting
  process for electric vehicle charging stations as required by Assembly Bill 1236 be
  adopted.

  2
 101  SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-031 APPROVED –
  CALIFORNIA CITIES GAMING AUTHORITY. Staff reported dated January 12,
  2021, was presented recommending an approval of a second amendment to Agreement
  No. 20-031 (the California Cities Gaming Authority Joint Exercise of Powers
  Agreement) to admit the City of San Jose as a Member.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Dotson, that
  the City Council does hereby approve the Second Amendment to Agreement No. 20-031.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AGREEMENT NO. 21- 082 APPROVED – GROW CYCLING FOUNDATION.
  Staff report dated January 12, 2021, was presented recommending approval of an
  agreement with Grow Cycling Foundation for the installation of a Pump Track at Edward
  Vincent Park at no cost.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-082. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEEMENT NO. 21-028 APPROVED – 40 LOVE
  FOUNDATION, INCORPORATED FOR TENNIS MANAGEMENT SERVICES.
  Staff report dated January 12, 2021, was presented recommending approval of
  Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 21-028 with 40 Love Foundation, Incorporated for
  Tennis Management Services to incorporate the hourly rate of one coaching staff not
  listed in the original agreement.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 21-
  028.The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

172  WAIVER AND GENERAL RELEASE APPROVED - RETIRED POLICE
  CANINE, ZORAN. Staff report dated January 12, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval of a waiver and general release for retired Police Canine, Zoran.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve a waiver and general release for retired Police
  Canine, Zoran. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 21-083 APPROVED – CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF
  TRANSPORTATION; RESOLUTION 21-46 ADOPTED – PROGRAM
  SUPPLEMENT NO. U42; RESOLUTION NO. 21-47 ADOPTED – AMENDMENT
  TO FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM (CIP)
  BUDGET. Staff report dated January 12, 2021, was presented recommending approval
  of an agreement with the California Department of Transportation.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-083; 2) Adopt
  Resolution No. 21-46 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE STATE
  PROGRAM SUPPLEMENT AGREEMENT NO. U42 AGREEMENT TO
  MASTER AGREEMENT NO. 00352S

  3
   and; 3) Adopt Resolution No. 21 – 47 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020-2021, ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  PROVIDE FUNDING FOR LOCAL ROADWAY SAFETY PLAN.

  The motion was carried out by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 21-087 APPROVED – MURPHY’S BOWL, LLC;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-48 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE 2020-2021 BUDGET.
  Staff report dated January 12, 2021, was presented recommending approval of an
  Advance Funding Agreement with Murphy’s Bowl, LLC (Developer) to fund the
  demolition of Inglewood Well No 6 in the total amount of $127,495 (includes $300 for
  project advertisement) for the Well No. 6 Destruction and Site Demolition project, per
  Bid. No. CB-20-13.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-087 in the amount of
  $127,495 and; 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-48 entitled :

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  RECEIVE FUNDS FROM MURPHY’S BOWL, LLC TO FINANCE THE
  DEMOLITION OF THE CITY’S WATER WELL NO.: 6.

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-086 APPROVED - BEST
  DRILLING AND PUMP , INC. Staff report dated January 12, 2021, was presented
  recommending award of contract and approval of an agreement with Best Drilling and
  Pump, Inc. to provide demolition services for the Well No. 6 Destruction and Site
  Demolition Project, per Bid No. CB-20-13.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 21-086 in
  an amount not to exceed $139,914.50 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in the
  amount of $12,719.50). The motion was carried out by following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Member Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – LABOR NEGOTIATIONS WITH SERVICE EMPLOYEES
  INTERNATIONAL  UNION  (SEIU);  INGLEWOOD  MANAGEMENT
  EMPLOYEE ORGANIZATION (IMEO); INGLEWOOD EXECUTIVE
  ORGANIZATION (IEO); INGLEWOOD POLICE OFFICERS ASSOCIATION
  (IPOA); INGLEWOOD POLICE MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION (IPMA);
  INGLEWOOD POLICE CIVILIAN MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION (IPCMA).
  Status was given to the City Council; Direction given to the staff.

127  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk, introduced the new staff
  in the City Clerk’s office, and thanked Mark and Dominique for their help with getting
  her office set up. She informed residents, who reside in the 30th Senate District, of a
  special election that will be held on March 2, 2021. She further stated that residents can
  drop their mail-in ballots off at Edward Vincent Park, and wished the residents a Happy
  New Year.

  4
 The City Clerk read an email regarding the Here to Stay Campaign on behalf of Inez
Torres from: Lourdes Amezcua, Jessica Saidman, Mary Car, Jennifer Bautista, M.B.,
Tierra (surname unkown), Danielle Carne, Mica Dregni, Francis Taylor, Amber Olmos,
Clara Leopo, and Luci Baker. The City Clerk asked the Mayor to adjourn the meeting in
honor of a long-term resident Mary Quick, and her aunt Virta Hawkins, who served as an
Inglewood poll worker.

PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons on the phone
who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

Ms. Craft, spoke regarding the Police Oversight Commission meeting, and wanting a
response to her calls and emails.

Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke concerning the funds.

Janice Ayala, an Inglewood resident, spoke on behalf of her mother Inez Torres
requesting a meeting with the City Council.

Eddie Cruz, spoke on behalf of Inez Torres and Sonia Alvarez requesting tenant and
home owner protection during the pandemic.

Tanisa Mantoro, spoke on behalf of Inez Torres and Sonia Alvarez wanting protection for
tenants and home owners in a crisis.

Brittany Morales, Here to Stay Campaign, requested minimum involvement from
Inglewood Police Department when tenants are being evicted.

Yvonne Diora, Los Angeles Voters Organizer, spoke on behalf of Sonia Alvarez and
asking the City Council Members to check their emails regarding this matter.

Lilian Lennox, Inglewood Tenants Union, spoke in regards to Inez Torres and her
property being taken after she was informed her mortgage payments were being
consolidated.

Irnerva (Last Name Unknown) spoke about Inez Torres and family, wanting protection
for renters and homeowners during this pandemic.

Mayor Butts read a commendation for Ervin Simonnette for his service to the country and
community.

There being no further business to be presented, Chairman Butts declared the meeting
adjourned in memory of Andrew Summerfield, Mary Quick, Perdita Brown, D.D. Brown,
Wife of Willie Brown, Virta Hawkins, aunt of City Clerk, Aisha Thompson, Art Lopez,
Rebecca Turner, Joe Sanders, and Danny Johnson at the hour of 2: 43 p.m.

Approved this 12th day of January, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

________________________
James Butts, Jr., Mayor
